title: Syllabus for Writing for the Social Sciences
summary: Writing course for social science students with a 'career builder' job-search writing unit, a literature review, a public awareness campaign, an informational interview and a portfolio. Readings are hyperlinked in the syllabus.

title: Writing for the Humanities and the Arts
assignment_type: syllabus, course calendar and grading contract
summary: Three-unit writing-in-the-disciplines course: students write op-eds, research a genre of their choice to build a 'genre guide' for others, then complete a multimodal project drawing on a genre guide. Includes the course calendar and a grading contract.
notes: Spring 2023, ENGL 210 at City College. License stated on record page. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 4.0 License'.

title: 21W.742 Writing About Race (Spring 2013)
pairs_with_readings: Cornel West, Race Matters
Toni Morrison, Jazz
Junot Diaz, The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao
Arundhati Roy, The God of Small Things
Toni Morrison, Nobel Lecture (1993)
summary: Writing course on how race and racial identity are constructed and represented in contemporary culture, using literature, essays, criticism and film. Sequence runs from descriptive and exploratory essays to an analytical midterm and a 10-page researched essay, with portfolio grading.
notes: 26 sessions (two 1.5-hour meetings a week). Readings are mostly copyrighted books and films. Closest MIT OCW match for a cultural-rhetorics-themed writing course, though framed as cultural criticism rather than cultural rhetorics. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)'.

title: 21W.777 Science Writing in Contemporary Society (Spring 2017)
pairs_with_readings: Elise Hancock, Ideas into Words: Mastering the Craft of Science Writing (recommended)
summary: Advanced undergraduate workshop in writing about science, technology, medicine and nature for contemporary audiences, reading essays, reportage, op-eds and web articles. Three essays with revision, a reading journal, an oral presentation and a portfolio.
notes: OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)'.

A service-learning component has students write grant proposals for community service projects.
notes: OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Good model for the community/service-learning FYC theme. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)'.

notes: OCW footer links CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Old (2002) but a clean grad-writing course design adaptable beyond management.

title: Textual Transformations: An Introduction to AI for Composition 101
source_repository: CUNY Academic Works (LaGuardia Community College OER)
summary: Roughly 20-hour, nine-lesson critical AI literacy unit for first-year composition covering what AI is, its history and workings, applications, academic integrity, ethics, AI in society and the relation of writing and AI. Each lesson pairs source exploration and inquiry with discussion and low-stakes writing; three essays and a revision/reflection essay sit at lessons 2, 5, 8 and 9.
notes: Spring 2025. Built for the CUNY Building Bridges of Knowledge program (Lumina Foundation). Shared as a PDF of Google Slides with teaching notes. Strongest openly licensed AI-and-writing course design found. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial 4.0 License'.

notes: Open to juniors, seniors and graduate students by placement. OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Required texts are commercial.

notes: 13 class days, five 3-hour sessions a week. OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Good multimodal science-communication course design.

summary: First major assignment for a business communication course: students build a resume, cover letter and LinkedIn page and develop three verbal narratives, each with a brief rubric, designed with Universal Design for Learning principles.
notes: Fall 2025. Worth 30% of the course grade. A second assignment from the same course (Unit 2, Key Concept Report) is at https://academicworks.cuny.edu/cc_oers/535. Not a full syllabus. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-Noncommercial-Share Alike 4.0 License'.

notes: OCW CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. Recommended handbooks are commercial. License as stated: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 License (CC BY-NC-SA 4.0)'.
